findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the concrete bridge-alert mechanism (the PUSH_PENDING-equivalent artifact/sentinel and where it is written) that strict mode emits on failure.
evidence: Body: 'Flip to non-red IF a PUSH_PENDING equivalent is added for the ephemeral context.'
AC2 says 'files a bridge alert' but the concrete artifact/channel/PUSH_PENDING sentinel is not defined
findings.finding: The strict-mode AC names 'files a bridge alert' but does not specify the alert mechanism/channel (the PUSH_PENDING-equivalent the body cites), leaving how fail-loud surfaces unspecified.
findings.location: AC2: "gains an explicit strict mode that exits non-zero AND files a bridge alert"
scenarios: Executor invents an alert shape that operators don't monitor, re-creating the silent-loss risk the plan set out to close

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and state explicitly whether reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:208-246's second CAS push loop is also collapsed into push.py or intentionally kept verbatim, and update its inline decision block (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:14-19) to match the reversal — not only the canary_bridge.py module docstring.
evidence: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:14-19: 'The final "flush unpushed" CAS push loop deliberately STAYS in YAML and is tested verbatim (ticket 4c4f's decision ...); do NOT migrate it into the module.'
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:208-246 is a second git push CAS loop with the same non-fast-forward classifier the plan attributes solely to reconcile-bridge.yml:272-377
canary_bridge.py:6-10: names BOTH 'the reconcile-bridge.yml commit-back CAS push loop' AND 'the canary flush (tickets-branch push retry loop)' as loops that 'must never absorb'
Plan AC updates the canary docstring for 'the reversal' but the reversal is scoped only to the reconcile-bridge loop
findings.finding: The plan overturns ticket 4c4f's 'CAS loop stays verbatim in YAML' decision but enumerates only ONE of the two YAML loops that decision governs. reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:208-246 contains a second 'flush unpushed' CAS push loop whose own inline standing-decision block (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:14-19, 'do NOT migrate it into the module', citing ticket 4c4f) is a peer of the reconcile-bridge.yml:285 marker the plan does list. The plan updates the canary_bridge.py module docstring but neither enumerates the canary workflow's inline decision block nor states whether the canary flush loop is also collapsed or intentionally left verbatim.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'The raw-git-ok marker, the canary docstring, and the push-retry test docstring are updated'
scenarios: Executor collapses reconcile-bridge.yml into push.py, updates canary_bridge.py docstring to reflect the reversal, but leaves reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:14-19 asserting a decision that is now half-overturned and leaves the canary's own flush loop diverging further
Reviewer of the follow-up asks why the canary flush loop still runs raw YAML git after the epic claimed to consolidate on 'one core entrypoint'

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the reconciler commit-back (git add -A && commit of uncommitted inbound events, currently reconcile-bridge.yml:290-293) is preserved when the YAML block is deleted — either extend push.py's entrypoint to commit dirty tree state first, or keep a minimal commit step in YAML ahead of the core call.
evidence: YAML step comment: 'the reconciler leaves inbound events UNCOMMITTED ... So we (a) commit any dirty state, then (b) push' (reconcile-bridge.yml:273-276)
reconcile-bridge.yml:290-293 runs `git add -A` + `git commit` before the push loop
push.py::push_tickets_branch (src/rebar/_store/push.py:228 onward) starts with `git push HEAD:branch`; there is no `git add`/`git commit` anywhere in the function
push.py also gates on `_push_mode` (off/async/always) and resolves branch/remote from config — none of which the CI entrypoint currently accounts for
findings.finding: The plan replaces the YAML block with push.py::push_tickets_branch but does not preserve the reconciler commit-back the block performs. The YAML does `git add -A && git commit` for the reconciler's UNCOMMITTED inbound events (reconcile-bridge.yml:290-293) BEFORE pushing; push.py::push_tickets_branch begins at the push step and assumes commits already exist — it never stages or commits a dirty tree. Deleting the block and calling push.py would push nothing when the reconciler left events uncommitted, silently losing exactly the events the loop exists to publish.
findings.location: AC line 'The 106-line YAML block is deleted; CI calls one core entrypoint'
scenarios: Reconciler applies inbound Jira events, leaves them staged/uncommitted, CI calls push.py which finds HEAD not ahead and pushes nothing — the events are lost with the ephemeral runner

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting strict mode exits non-zero AND files a bridge alert when retries are exhausted (a rejected/unresolvable CAS push), so the fail-loud disposition-flip guarantee is tested, not just the happy-path entrypoint invocation.
evidence: The plan states strict mode is the condition for flipping the disposition: 'Flip to non-red IF a PUSH_PENDING equivalent is added' and 'Without a fail-loud mode, replacing the YAML loop with best-effort push.py silently converts a red into a silent loss.'

The re-homed contention test covers 'the same failure modes' and the smoke tests assert 'the entrypoint is actually invoked' — neither is stated to assert strict-mode exit code + alert emission on exhausted retries.
findings.finding: The plan adds a new strict mode (exit non-zero AND file a bridge alert) whose entire purpose is to prevent silent loss on a rejected CAS push, but no acceptance criterion names a test that exercises that fail-loud path — that strict mode actually exits non-zero and files the alert when a push cannot be completed.
findings.location: AC: 'push.py gains an explicit strict mode that exits non-zero AND files a bridge alert'
scenarios: Strict mode ships with a bug (e.g. swallows the non-zero exit or skips the alert); the suite goes green because no test asserts the fail-loud behavior, and the exact silent-loss regression the ticket exists to prevent reaches CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A test drives push.py in strict mode against an unresolvable rejection and asserts a non-zero exit code plus an emitted bridge alert.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the reconciled retry budget explicitly (e.g. adopt the YAML's 5+final-push) with a one-line rationale, rather than leaving 'reconciled' undefined.
evidence: Body: 'YAML: 5 retries + a final push', 'push.py: 3 retries'
'Ticket 4c4f's own acceptance criteria has an UNCHECKED item: reconcile the budgets (it uses 3, the workflow 5).'
AC states 'the retry budgets are reconciled' without naming the target number
findings.finding: The retry-budget reconciliation AC does not decide which budget wins (push.py's 3 vs YAML's 5); it defers the exact choice 4c4f left unchecked.
scenarios: Executor must pick 3 or 5 with no stated rationale and may pick the wrong one for the ephemeral context
findings.suggested_fix: Name the winning budget and why — e.g. 'push.py adopts 5 retries + a final push, matching the workflow's stronger resilience.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/extend an AC so CI invokes push.py in strict mode AND a test exercises strict-mode fail-loud (non-zero exit + alert) on a simulated exhausted-retry, proving the production path fails loud.
evidence: Body: 'replacing the YAML loop with best-effort push.py silently converts a red into a silent loss.'
AC3 requires CI calls the entrypoint but does not require it be the strict-mode invocation
'one thin smoke test per provider asserting the entrypoint is actually invoked' asserts invocation, not strict-mode/fail-loud behavior
findings.finding: No AC requires CI to invoke push.py IN strict mode; the AC set could be satisfied (entrypoint invoked, strict mode exists) while CI still calls best-effort mode — reproducing the silent-loss the plan warns against.
findings.location: AC3 "CI calls one core entrypoint" + AC2 strict mode
scenarios: Reviewer sees green: entrypoint invoked + strict mode implemented + smoke test passes, yet CI wired to best-effort default → the red-to-silent-loss regression ships

findings.checklist_item: State which retry budget the reconciled push.py uses (and the rationale, referencing 4c4f's contention model) rather than leaving 'reconcile the budgets' to implementer choice.
evidence: push.py: `_MAX_RETRIES = 3` (src/rebar/_store/push.py:66)
YAML: `max_retries=5` (reconcile-bridge.yml:310)
4c4f model: per-attempt loss 35/54/72/88%, giving P(all five fail) ~12%/run — attempt count is the convergence lever
Plan: 'the retry budgets are reconciled (it uses 3, the workflow 5)' states the discrepancy but not the resolution
findings.finding: The retry-budget reconciliation is under-specified in a load-bearing dimension. 4c4f's own Poisson model ties convergence probability directly to attempt count (P(all fail) ~12% at the old cadence), and the two paths differ (YAML 5, push.py 3). The plan says 'reconcile the budgets' but never states which value survives or the basis for choosing — yet after the final-push fix is ported, the attempt count is precisely what determines whether normal contention still exhausts.
findings.location: AC line "4c4f's final-push fix is ported into push.py and the retry budgets are reconciled"
scenarios: Budgets reconciled downward to 3 in the shared path: CI convergence under contention regresses versus the 5-attempt YAML loop the fix was validated against
